The curve rises as the volume of NaOH increases, and equivalence points appear in two obvious steep vertical rising regions; these equivalence points correspond to specific NaOH volumes on the horizontal axis of the graph. Reasoning: When the titration is repeated, the carbonic acid sample remains unchanged, so the amount of substance of NaOH required to reach each equivalence point remains unchanged. According to n = MV, when the required amount of substance of NaOH n remains unchanged and the NaOH concentration M increases, the required volume V = n/M will decrease. Therefore, the two equivalence points on the graph will both appear at smaller NaOH volumes, that is, shift to the left.
